high.title: Investors React to Vale (VALE3), Santander (SANB11) Earnings and Selic Cut; Ibovespa in Dollars Rises Today (29)
high.summary: This is "Super Wednesday" with dual monetary policy decisions from Brazil's COPOM and the US Federal Reserve. The market overwhelmingly expects Brazil to continue its monetary easing cycle with a 0.25 percentage point cut to the Selic rate, reducing it from 14.75% to 14.50% annually. In contrast, the FOMC is expected to keep US rates steady between 3.50%-3.75%. The Fed meeting carries additional significance as it may be Jerome Powell's final meeting before his mandate expires May 15th. Investors are also digesting earnings results, with Vale (VALE3) reporting Q1 net profit of US$1.9 billion, up 36% year-over-year. The dual policy decisions amid Middle East tensions and rising oil prices create a critical juncture for BRL positioning and Brazilian asset flows. A Selic cut would widen the rate differential with the US, potentially pressuring the Real, while Vale's strong results support the mining-heavy Ibovespa.

high.title: Former BC Official Diogo Guillen Assumes Chief Economist Position at Itaú Unibanco
high.summary: Itaú Unibanco announced a significant change in its Economic Research leadership, with Diogo Guillen set to become the bank's new chief economist starting July 1st after completing his quarantine period. Guillen brings recent experience from Brazil's Central Bank, where he served as Economic Policy Director from 2022-2025, and previously worked in Itaú's asset management economic area from 2015-2021. He holds a PhD from Princeton University. Guillen replaces Mário Mesquita, who leaves after nearly a decade leading Macroeconomics and Research since July 2016. Mesquita's departure follows the bank's internal mandatory retirement rule for management positions at age 60. This leadership change at Brazil's largest private bank signals continuity in institutional knowledge given Guillen's Central Bank experience during the recent tightening cycle. His appointment could influence Itaú's economic forecasting and strategic positioning, particularly relevant given current monetary policy transitions and market expectations for further Selic cuts.

medium.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Retakes $77,000 Before US Interest Rate Decision; See Cryptocurrency Prices This Wednesday (29)
medium.summary: Bitcoin trades above $77,000 with 1% gains ahead of the US Fed decision. The cryptocurrency market rises in anticipation of Super Wednesday, with Brazil's COPOM expected to cut Selic by 0.25pp to 14.50% while the US Fed likely holds rates steady at 3.50%-3.75%. This divergence could impact crypto flows and BRL positioning.

medium.title: Braskem (BRKM5) Receives Board Nominations from Novonor and Petrobras (PETR4), Including Magda Chambriard
medium.summary: Braskem receives new board nominations including Petrobras CEO Magda Chambriard as board president and Novonor CEO Héctor Nuñez as vice-president for Wednesday's shareholder meeting. This follows last week's announcement of Novonor's agreement to sell control of the petrochemical company to Shine I FIP fund, representing significant corporate governance changes at Brazil's largest petrochemical company.

medium.title: Banco do Brasil (BBAS3) Diagnosis for Agribusiness: 'If Selic Falls, the Sector Reacts Quickly'
medium.summary: Banco do Brasil's agribusiness VP expects the sector to respond quickly to continued Selic cuts. With a R$406 billion agribusiness portfolio, the bank sees lower rates as favorable for new investments and debt restructuring. BB projects R$3 billion in business at Agrishow, highlighting the agricultural sector's sensitivity to monetary policy changes and potential benefits from today's expected rate cut.

medium.title: Ibovespa Rally Doesn't Eliminate 'Invisible Risk': Meet Empiricus's New Global Allocation Portfolio to 'Shield' Your Portfolio
medium.summary: Despite geopolitical uncertainties, the Ibovespa has gained 20% this year, reaching a new high near 198,000 points. Foreign capital inflows of R$50 billion in Q1 and expectations of Selic cuts support the rally. However, the research house warns of "invisible risks" for concentrated domestic positioning, launching a global allocation portfolio for diversification amid the strong local market performance.
